historical_references.reference: The concept of Qadr is rooted in the early Islamic period, specifically in the teachings of Imam Ali Zainul Abidin (570-661 AD) as recorded in his Hadith Al-Ghadeer. This Hadith emphasizes the importance of predestination and that 'Whatever Allah has written for anyone will come to pass', indicating the belief in divine decree and the role of Qadr in shaping human lives.

historical_references.reference: The term 'Qadr' gained prominence during the period of the Abbasid Caliphate (750-1258 AD) when theologians and scholars debated the nature and extent of divine predestination and human free will. The concept became a central theme in Islamic theology, and various theories such as Jabriyah (determinism), Qadariyah (free-willism), and Murjiah (negation of human action) emerged in response to these debates.
